# std.rand

Random numbers from a seed: the same seed gives the same numbers in `cpl run` and in the built C++. `Rng(seed)` is a splitmix64 stream: O(1) per draw.

Import: `use std.rand.{...}`.

## `struct Rng(s: U64)`

- `fn new(seed: Int) -> Rng` — O(1); A deterministic stream of random bits seeded by `seed`.
- `fn next(mut self) -> U64` — O(1); The next 64 random bits: one splitmix64 step.
- `fn int(mut self, lo: Int, hi: Int) -> Int` — O(1); A uniformly random integer in `lo..=hi`, both ends inclusive, from one `next()`.; traps: when `lo > hi`
- `fn float(mut self) -> F64` — O(1); A uniformly random `F64` in `[0, 1)`: the top 53 bits of `next()` times `2^-53`.
- `fn chance(mut self, p: F64) -> Bool` — O(1); True with probability `p`: `float() < p`.
- `fn pick<S: Indexed, T>(mut self, xs: S) -> ?T` — O(1); A uniformly random element of `xs`: `xs` at position `int(0..xs.len)`.
- `fn shuffle<S: IndexedMut>(mut self, mut a: S)` — O(n); Shuffle `a` in place, uniformly (Fisher-Yates).
- `fn perm<D>(mut self) -> [D]D` — O(n); A uniformly random permutation of the domain `D`, as a `[D]D`.
- `fn sample<S: Indexed, T>(mut self, k: Int, from: S) -> List<T>` — O(|from|); `k` elements of `from` at distinct positions, chosen uniformly, in random order.; traps: when `k` is not in `0..=from.len`

## Example

```cp
use std.rand.{Rng}
var rng = Rng(42)
let x = rng.int(1, 10)
assert 1 <= x <= 10
```
